title: Stabilize one launch-scale CUPTI comparison with inner iterations
objective: Determine whether a microsecond-scale candidate is a real paired win when two-iteration CUPTI samples have excessive ratio spread.
preconditions: An otherwise gate-eligible paired run whose timing spread exceeds the configured limit
steps: Preserve the same candidate, shapes, warmup, repeat count, cold-L2 policy, and adjacent order-balanced pairs
Increase only the inner iterations used to form each sample median
Rerun the complete canonical sweep and inspect p10, regressions, pair-ratio spread, and unseen-seed correctness
Record both the unstable diagnostic and stable rerun; never discard the first result

acceptance.pass: Every shape is correct, at least one wins, none regress, and all pair-ratio spreads are within the declared stability limit.
acceptance.no_verdict: The automatic retry or higher-inner-iteration run remains unstable.
acceptance.no_win: The stable conservative ratios remove the apparent speedup or expose a regression.

stop_rule: After one higher-inner-iteration rerun, accept its terminal state; do not tune sampling parameters repeatedly to manufacture a verdict.
origin_evidence: router_jit_gemm was UNSTABLE_NO_VERDICT at iterations=2, then passed the unchanged full gate at iterations=30 with M16 p10=2.712x and spread=1.010x.
